name: IELTS Speaking Vocabulary
description: Từ và cụm từ tự nhiên cho IELTS Speaking Part 1–3, gồm mô tả, sở thích, trải nghiệm, ý kiến, so sánh, nguyên nhân, ví dụ và cách nối ý. Ưu tiên ngôn ngữ nói tự nhiên thay vì học thuộc bài mẫu.

words.example: My daily routine is fairly simple on weekdays.
words.note: Useful for Part 1 topics about study, work, and daily life.

words.example: My commute is much shorter than it used to be.
words.note: Useful for work, study, and transport topics.

words.mean: hộ gia đình; việc gia đình
words.example: Everyone in my household helps with chores.
words.note: Useful for home and family topics.

words.mean: thời gian rảnh; hoạt động giải trí
words.example: I usually read during my leisure time.
words.note: Useful formal noun for free-time discussions.

words.example: Listening to music is one of my favourite pastimes.
words.note: Natural alternative to hobby in some contexts.

words.example: I usually listen to music to unwind after school.
words.note: Natural speaking verb for relaxing after a busy day.

words.example: I sometimes catch up with my friends at the weekend.
words.note: Very useful for friends and socialising topics.

words.example: I like socialising with people who share my interests.
words.note: British spelling commonly used in IELTS.

words.example: It was a memorable trip because I travelled with my family.
words.note: Useful for Part 2 stories and experiences.

words.example: My preference is to study in the morning.
words.note: Useful when comparing choices and giving reasons.

words.example: I am quite keen on documentaries.
words.note: Natural phrase for likes and interests.

words.example: I have always been fond of old songs.
words.note: Useful for expressing long-term preferences.

words.example: I tend to study better when it is quiet.
words.note: Useful for describing habits without sounding absolute.

words.example: I eat out from time to time.
words.note: Natural frequency phrase for Part 1.

words.example: I watch a film once in a while.
words.note: Natural alternative to sometimes.

words.example: I usually review vocabulary before bed.
words.note: Useful but basic; combine with more specific details.

words.example: My hometown is fairly quiet at night.
words.note: Useful for moderate descriptions.

words.example: I particularly enjoy listening to live music.
words.note: Useful for adding precise emphasis.

words.example: I genuinely enjoy learning about different cultures.
words.note: Useful for sounding natural when expressing real enthusiasm.

words.example: Admittedly, public transport can be crowded at rush hour.
words.note: Useful for balanced responses in Part 3.

words.example: Personally, I prefer working in a small team.
words.note: Natural way to signal a personal view.

words.example: I suppose the main reason is convenience.
words.note: Useful for softening an opinion naturally.

words.example: I'd say my hometown is fairly peaceful.
words.note: Natural way to answer without sounding memorised.

words.example: What I like about my school is the friendly atmosphere.
words.note: Useful for giving a reason for a preference.

words.example: One thing that stands out is the city's food culture.
words.note: Useful for describing memorable features.

words.example: It depends on how much free time I have.
words.note: Useful for nuanced Part 3 answers.

words.example: Compared with my old school, my current school is larger.
words.note: Useful for direct personal comparisons.

words.example: I enjoy outdoor activities, especially cycling.
words.note: Natural emphasis word for examples.

words.example: I would absolutely recommend visiting my hometown.
words.note: Strong emphasis; use when genuine.

words.example: I would definitely choose the train for a long journey.
words.note: Natural emphatic adverb.

words.example: I would probably spend more time outdoors if I could.
words.note: Useful for hypothetical and uncertain answers.

words.example: Ideally, I would like to study abroad one day.
words.note: Useful for future plans and preferences.

words.example: I enjoy spontaneous trips when my schedule allows.
words.note: Useful for describing personality and travel.

words.example: Online shopping is convenient because it saves time.
words.note: High-frequency adjective for daily-life topics.

words.example: The café is affordable for students.
words.note: Useful for money, shopping, housing, and travel topics.

words.mean: dễ tiếp cận; dễ sử dụng
words.example: The library is easily accessible by bus.
words.note: Useful for transport, services, and technology topics.

words.example: The city centre is lively at night.
words.note: Useful for describing places and atmospheres.

words.example: I prefer living in a peaceful neighbourhood.
words.note: Useful for hometown and home topics.

words.example: The market gets very crowded at weekends.
words.note: Useful for city, transport, and travel topics.

words.example: The route is scenic, especially near the coast.
words.note: Useful for travel and hometown descriptions.

words.example: The mountain view was absolutely breathtaking.
words.note: Useful for strong positive descriptions in Part 2.

words.example: I find space exploration fascinating.
words.note: Useful for describing subjects, people, and experiences.

words.example: Learning to speak confidently was challenging at first.
words.note: Useful for experiences and personal development.

words.mean: đáng giá; đem lại cảm giác thành tựu
words.example: Volunteering can be challenging but very rewarding.
words.note: Useful for work, study, and activities.

words.example: Exams can be stressful if I do not prepare well.
words.note: Useful for study, work, and modern-life topics.

words.example: Moving to a huge city can feel overwhelming at first.
words.note: Useful for strong negative or mixed feelings.

words.example: Regular exercise is beneficial for my health.
words.note: Useful for Part 3 when discussing effects.

words.example: Let me think; I would probably choose the countryside.
words.note: Natural stalling phrase; use sparingly.

words.example: To be honest, I do not spend much time watching television.
words.note: Useful for natural personal answers.

words.example: As far as I remember, the library opened about ten years ago.
words.note: Useful when recalling details in Part 2.

words.example: What I mean is that I prefer a quieter environment.
words.note: Useful for self-correction and clarification.

words.example: The main reason is that it saves me a lot of time.
words.note: Useful for extending answers with a reason.

words.example: For instance, I often use podcasts to practise listening.
words.note: Useful for supporting an example naturally.

words.example: On the whole, I am happy with my current routine.
words.note: Useful summary phrase for longer answers.

words.example: In other words, I prefer quality to quantity.
words.note: Useful for paraphrasing or clarifying.

words.example: That said, I still think public transport needs improvement.
words.note: Useful for balanced Part 3 responses.

words.example: It is convenient, but at the same time it can be expensive.
words.note: Useful for presenting two sides.

words.example: If I had to choose, I would pick the countryside.
words.note: Natural way to answer comparison questions.

words.example: From my point of view, schools should teach practical skills.
words.note: Useful in Part 3; avoid repeating it mechanically.

words.example: In my experience, group work can improve communication.
words.note: Useful for personal examples.

words.word: a good example of this is
words.mean: một ví dụ điển hình là
words.example: A good example of this is our school recycling project.
words.note: Useful when developing a Part 3 point.

words.mean: một lý do cho điều này là
words.example: One reason for this is that people are more connected online.
words.note: Useful for causal explanation.

words.mean: ở một mức độ nào đó
words.example: To some extent, social media has changed how people communicate.
words.note: Useful for nuanced agreement or partial support.

words.example: In the long run, learning to manage money is very useful.
words.note: Useful for consequences and future effects.

words.example: Even small lifestyle changes can make a difference.
words.note: Useful for impact and solutions.

words.example: Technology has a major impact on how students learn.
words.note: Core phrase for discussing effects.

words.mean: coi điều gì là hiển nhiên
words.example: People sometimes take clean water for granted.
words.note: Useful advanced phrase for social and environmental topics.

words.example: Travelling can broaden my horizons.
words.note: Natural phrase for travel, education, and experiences.

words.word: step out of my comfort zone
words.mean: bước ra khỏi vùng an toàn
words.example: Giving a presentation helped me step out of my comfort zone.
words.note: Useful for personal development and challenge topics.

words.example: I use messaging apps to keep in touch with my cousins.
words.note: Useful for technology and relationships topics.

words.example: I get along well with my classmates.
words.note: Useful for friends, family, and school topics.

words.example: I have a soft spot for old cartoons.
words.note: Natural idiomatic phrase; use only when it feels natural.

words.example: Horror films are not really my cup of tea.
words.note: Natural but informal; suitable for Speaking, not formal Writing.
